chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

As for what the earth produces of any of the things, there is no zakat in it except in four things: wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. And there is no zakat in any of these four things until it reaches five awsiq. The wasq is sixty sa', and it is three hundred sa' by the sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). If there are five awsiq of each kind, there is [zakat]; if it is less, there is no zakat. And if the wheat, barley, dates, and raisins decrease, or if one sa' or part of a sa' is less than five awsiq, there is no zakat. If it is cultivated with effort (watering by carrying water), then half the tithe (2.5%) is due; and if it is watered without effort, by a river or otherwise, or by rain, then the full tithe (5%) is due.

key_terms.أَوْسَاقٍ: Awsaq (plural of wasq, a unit of volume/weight)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and rates for zakat on agricultural produce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that zakat on crops is limited to these four staple grains and fruits, establishing the nisab at five awsiq (approximately 300 sa's). It distinguishes the zakat rate based on irrigation effort: a full tithe (10%) for natural watering and half a tithe (5%) for irrigated crops, reflecting the economic burden on the farmer. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for agricultural taxation and is often linked to the concept of 'Ushr' in the Quran.
